article.title: Unpatched Cacti Zero-Day Enables RCE in Just Four HTTP Requests via Guest Access
article.summary: Details have emerged about a new zero-day vulnerability in Cacti, an open-source network monitoring tool, that could be exploited to achieve remote code execution. The proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit, which has yet to be assigned a CVE identifier, has been tracked as 4HTTP2SHELL and 4HTTP2ROOT. article.title: SAP Confirms Cyberattack, Source Code Reportedly Compromised
article.summary: SAP has detected suspicious activity on GitHub, where hackers reportedly used stolen employee tokens to copy and alter source code. The post SAP Confirms Cyberattack, Source Code Reportedly Compromised appeared first on SecurityWeek .

items.relevance_reason: Tập đoàn phần mềm SAP xác nhận sự cố an ninh mạng khi kẻ tấn công lợi dụng mã token của nhân viên trên GitHub để sao chép và chỉnh sửa mã nguồn.

article.title: Critical Juniper Session Smart Conductor Flaw Exploited in Attacks
article.summary: Tracked as CVE-2026-103406, the vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root. The post Critical Juniper Session Smart Conductor Flaw Exploited in Attacks appeared first on SecurityWeek .

items.relevance_reason: Lỗ hổng nghiêm trọng CVE-2026-103406 trên Juniper Session Smart Conductor đang bị khai thác thực tế cho phép thực thi lệnh từ xa với quyền root.

article.title: Switzerland Confirms AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Breached Critical Infrastructure Operators
article.summary: Attackers using AI agents have broken into computer systems at Swiss organizations in four of five confirmed attacks, the first such cases in the country, the country's cybersecurity agency said yesterday. article.title: Chinese and North Korean state hackers add ARTEX AI framework to their arsenal
article.summary: State-sponsored hacking groups tied to Beijing and Pyongyang have started running the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft Threat Intelligence warned this week. Published on GitHub in July 2026 by a user going by Autumn-27, ARTEX is an LLM-driven open-source penetration testing framework that runs attacks largely on its own, with the operator setting a goal and AI agents planning and carrying out the steps needed to reach it.
